checks.finding: Every in-scope Goal (REQ-001..REQ-006, requirements.md '## Goals') states concrete, checkable conditions: REQ-001 names the exact suite file, the six PATH-availability/precedence branches, and both --emit modes; REQ-002 names the exact 3-class x 4-runtime x 3-tool_name-shape matrix; REQ-003 names the closed greenfield|brownfield field and the 10 mapped scenario classes; REQ-004 names the byte-unchanged required-checks needs: list and the [deterministic] prefix convention; REQ-005 names the exact registration files (run-all.sh/.ps1, test.yml via human-copy); REQ-006 names concrete bash-3.2/ps1-ASCII hygiene rules and per-issue CHANGELOG entries. A downstream task author or verifier can validate each without further clarification.

Every Goal has a 1:1-labeled acceptance-criterion block: REQ-001->AC-001..007, REQ-002->AC-008..011, REQ-003->AC-012..015, REQ-004->AC-016..018, REQ-005->AC-019..020, REQ-006->AC-021..023 (requirements.md '## Acceptance Criteria', each line ends with its owning '(REQ-NNN)' tag). acceptance-tests.md's table mirrors AC-NNN 1:1 as TEST-NNN with no gaps or extra unmapped rows.

Acceptance criteria describe externally observable outcomes rather than intent: AC-005's exit 2 / copilot-shaped deny JSON, AC-006's marker-writing-stub precedence proof, AC-011's explicit cross-runtime decision-agreement check, AC-017's text-marker self-check enumerating every pre-change step name against the staged candidate, AC-019/AC-020's grep-based registration self-checks, and AC-022's CHANGELOG-entry-count check. Each names a concrete artifact, exit code, or comparison a verifier can execute without inferring intent.

requirements.md '## Non-goals' is explicit and specific: excludes direct edits to the 4 genuinely R-10-protected suites, inventing a new fixture-profile vocabulary instead of ADR-0010's, migrating/renaming tests/scenario.tests.sh, treating Stream D as a fix for a currently-mixed lane, anything in epic #136 Phase 4 (#128-#135) or the design-sync issues (#138-#140), any test.yml human-copy staging beyond the ONE shared batch this feature produces, and tasks.md/traceability.md/traceability.json. Each boundary is tied to a concrete file or issue-number scope, not left implicit.

The human-copy staging/approval-boundary constraint for the ONE shared test.yml batch is stated with a real internal contradiction. Six passages state the batch carries all FOUR streams' edits: AC-020 ('the ONE shared batch, Streams A + B + C + D'), Non-goals ('Stream C registers its runner via the same explicit-step rule, inside this ONE shared batch'), Main Workflows item 3 (Stream C: 'stage its CI step via human-copy -- inside this feature's ONE shared staged batch'), the CI role description ('the ONE shared staged test.yml candidate (Streams A + B + C + D)'), Assumptions ('Streams A/B/C/D's test.yml edits'), and OQ-4 ('the ONE shared staged batch ... carries Streams A/B/C/D's test.yml edits'). But three other passages were not swept to match: the Roles and Permissions Agent bullet describes the batch as only 'Stream A's and Stream B's new CI steps plus Stream D's step-prefix lane marking' (Stream C omitted); the Security Boundaries table's B3 row repeats the identical 3-stream description ('the ONE shared staged batch (Streams A's/B's new CI steps and Stream D's step-prefix lane marking)'); and the Risks section's Medium intra-batch risk states 'Streams A, B, and D all stage edits to the SAME protected .github/workflows/test.yml file' and requires the design to 'carry all three streams' edits coherently' -- while citing '(Non-goals/OQ-4)' as its own source, even though Non-goals/OQ-4 both actually describe FOUR streams. Downstream failure mode: this Risks paragraph is the passage that motivates design.md's Global Constraints to name 'the exact internal ordering of edits within that one reviewed diff' (Main Workflows item 4); if a design author trusts this paragraph's own stream count, Stream C's CI-step edit position within the shared candidate could be left unordered/unaddressed, reintroducing the exact intra-batch merge hazard the paragraph exists to close. This is specification review's responsibility because it is a plain textual contradiction discoverable by reading requirements.md alone, before any design or task-decomposition work begins -- exactly the residue this attempt's stated 'four consistency edits' were supposed to eliminate. Major (not Critical) because the contradiction is confined to 3 narrative/supporting passages against 6 unambiguous authoritative ones (including the binding AC-020), so the document is not unreviewable as a whole, but a task/design author relying specifically on the Risks or Roles-and-Permissions passage would be missing load-bearing scope detail.

Every risk in requirements.md '## Risks' ties to a planned validation surface: the retired ADR-0010 risk cites the Stream C status record as its resolution evidence; the Medium intra-batch risk cites design.md's Global Constraints as the planned ordering mechanism; the Stream B 12-combination risk cites AC-008/009/010's explicit per-combination enumeration and acceptance-tests.md's TEST-ID traceability table; the Low-Medium PATH-stub false-pass risk cites the Edge Cases requirement that each fixture assert genuine tool absence/presence before asserting on the guard decision; the Low Stream D step-drop/needs-list risk cites AC-017's text-marker self-check plus an explicit human reviewer verification step before the candidate is applied.
